Temperature dependent ARPES suggests possible band splitting as the materials undergo magnetic transitions, helping to understand the magnetic interactions. Our results point to their likely magnetic topological insulating nature.

title: SeriesXRD: automated reflection tracking and phase identification in high-pressure X-ray diffraction series
summary: High-pressure synchrotron X-ray diffraction increasingly produces hundreds to thousands of detector frames in a single experiment, while separating, assigning, and tracking weak reflections across an entire series often remain manual. This bottleneck is particularly severe for micron- and nanoscale samples in diamond-anvil cells, where scattering from the anvils, gasket, pressure medium, and pressure markers can dominate the sample signal. We present SeriesXRD, an open-source workflow that analyzes diffraction as a series rather than as independent patterns. The program suppresses azimuthally localized diamond scattering, subtracts background, fits and tracks reflections between frames, matches known phases using pressure-dependent lattice parameters, subtracts confidently assigned contributions, and groups persistent unexplained reflections for follow-up as candidate sample-associated or unknown-phase features. We demonstrate the method on 1288 frames collected from an approximately 30-nm-thick layered UOTe flake in a diamond-anvil cell over 3.5-50.7 GPa. The dataset is strongly background dominated, with detectable UOTe diffraction in only approximately 4% of the frames. SeriesXRD recovered the sample-associated reflections identified in the original manual analysis while reducing the corresponding phase-assignment and residual-analysis workflow from more than two months of researcher time to an overnight automated run. Across the full series, 17,143 peaks were fitted, 14,395 passed quality criteria, and 90% of accepted peaks were assigned to known background or reference phases. SeriesXRD therefore converts large, background-dominated diffraction series into a tractable set of phase assignments and coherent unexplained reflections while retaining a traceable record of each decision.

title: Beyond Synthesis Conditions: Linking In-situ Growth Dynamics to Carbon Nanotube Forest Properties through Multimodal Machine Learning
summary: Machine learning for chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) has largely mapped static synthesis conditions to final properties, implicitly treating these conditions as a complete description of growth. Here, we test this assumption by integrating gas-flow conditions with in-situ time-resolve growth profiles (growth curves) of vertically aligned CNT forests. We introduce an observation-window analysis, in which prediction is evaluated as a function of observation time by providing models with the growth curve only up to progressively later times, to determine not only whether a property can be predicted, but when the necessary information becomes available during synthesis. Clustering of normalized growth curves revealed distinct growth patterns independent of final forest height. The gas conditions alone could predict the initial growth rate but not the growth lifetime and failed to capture the variation in yield (R^2<0). Adding the growth curve improved yield prediction (R^2~0.4-0.5), with the relevant information emerging during the intermediate and later stages of growth rather than at its onset. In contrast, density and G/D ratio, which forest height does not record, showed no consistent improvement. The maximum height and lifetime could be estimated with moderate accuracy midway through the 10-min growth. Permutation feature importance identified water vapor and H_2, both linked to catalyst activity, as the most informative gas variables. These results indicate that variation unexplained by synthesis conditions is not merely noise but reflects an evolving catalyst state, and they establish mid-growth decision points for autonomous synthesis, enabling early termination of unpromising batches and, ultimately, in-batch adjustment of growth conditions.

title: IRIS: an agentic eye on symmetry-derived paths and energy landscapes of structural phase transitions
summary: Structural phase transitions underpin ferroelectric and multiferroic functionality, but constructing interpretable energy landscapes remains dependent on specialist expertise. Predicting this behaviour rests on Landau free energies expanded in symmetry-adapted order parameters: their coefficients classify a transition, expose the couplings between distortions, set switching paths and barriers, and parametrize phase-field and effective-Hamiltonian models at larger scales. Obtaining these coefficients from first principles means sampling the Born--Oppenheimer energy surface along symmetry-derived structural paths, which requires crystallographic analysis, reliable structure generation and extensive computation, especially for coupled multidimensional order parameters. Here we introduce IRIS, an agentic workflow that converts plain-language requests and crystal structures into symmetry-adapted energy landscapes and fitted Landau energy models. Deterministic gates govern acceptance of structures, calculations and fits, while language models interpret requests and select constrained recovery actions. Applications across six compounds include a six-dimensional BiFeO$_3$ landscape that separates competition between polar and tilt amplitudes from directional locking and ranks homogeneous switching pathways. Controlled replays detected all 53 injected faults; disabling gates allowed 14 silent errors. Four prospective BaTiO$_3$ runs produced fitted landscapes from 96 density-functional calculations in 34 minutes total without intervening human decisions. IRIS makes physical model construction a reusable computational capability and provides a framework for scientific automation grounded in explicit verification.

title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
summary: Crystal-generation models can explore compositions and atomic arrangements beyond a fixed set of crystal prototypes, but their usefulness for a specific materials family depends on whether the generated structures retain the defining topology and whether their predicted properties remain reliable across the sampled chemistry. Here, a pretrained diffusion model is used to generate candidate ABX$_3$ perovskites and to examine their structural, chemical and electronic-property distributions. A connectivity-based filter distinguishes three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskites from structures that share the same nominal ABX$_3$ stoichiometry. The accepted set contains substantial B-site multiplicity, including ordered double-perovskite configurations that are inaccessible to the two-prototype substitution reference used here. The generated set is enriched in chloride-, bromide- and iodide-containing compositions relative to the Materials Project, while all generated B-site elements are already represented in that database. On the downstream MP-trained ALIGNN scale, the predicted bandgap distribution is shifted towards 1.4 eV, but the target-window fraction (8.2\%) is close to the MP reference fraction (7.3\%); the separate MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent this comparison from establishing target-condition enrichment. An ALIGNN model performs well on a formula-grouped random test split but does not outperform a constant baseline on a deliberately severe B-site-disjoint test. First-principles calculations on six generated structures show that relaxation can alter structural classification and that predicted and calculated gaps can differ appreciably. These results identify both the chemical-space coverage offered by crystal diffusion and the structural and predictive checks needed before its outputs can be treated as materials candidates.

title: Radiofrequency plasma spheroidization of lightweight complex concentrated superalloy Al10Nb20Ta15Ti30V5Zr20
summary: Recent advances in additive manufacturing (AM) have significantly increased the demand for high-quality metal powders with tailored composition. For refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCA) preparing such powders by conventional metallurgical method remains challenging due to their high melting point and chemical reactivity. In this paper, we present a method to produce spherical RCCA powders (here Al10Nb20Ta15Ti30V5Zr20) via mechanical alloying followed by radio-frequency inductively coupled plasma spheroidization. The resulting powder is suitable for AM processes because of its spherical morphology and a microstructure consisting of major BCC phases with local B2 phase. Complex carbide formation was studied by 3D atom probe tomography.

title: Efficient Interpolation of the Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian at Arbitrary Momenta
summary: We develop an efficient reciprocal-space method to reconstruct the static Bethe-Salpeter (BSE) Hamiltonian at arbitrary crystal momenta from coarse first-principles grids. Bloch states are interpolated within an optimally smooth Wannier subspace, while the screened Coulomb interaction is reconstructed from the dielectric response. This decouples the electron-hole transition momenta and transferred momentum from the underlying ab initio sampling. We benchmark the method on monolayer hBN, monolayer MoS$_2$, and bulk GaAs against explicit ab initio calculations, finding excellent agreement for dense-grid Bloch states, dielectric screening, and BSE optical spectra. Furthermore, our cost analysis estimates speedups of up to $22\times$ on the grids considered here. Arbitrary transferred-momentum sampling gives direct access to the long-wavelength exciton dispersion: in hBN and MoS$_2$, we resolve the nonanalytic behaviour induced by long-range electron-hole exchange at momenta well below the spacing of practical uniform grids. For bulk GaAs, locally refined transition-momentum sampling yields a converged binding energy for the threefold-degenerate lowest exciton, in close agreement with experiment and reference calculations, using far fewer BSE points than conventional uniform meshes. As the present framework provides exciton energies and amplitudes at arbitrary crystal momenta, it opens the way to incorporating ab initio excitonic effects into nonlocal electron-phonon vertices and to extensions towards exciton-phonon interactions and nonequilibrium exciton dynamics.

title: Ab Initio strain-dependent vibrational analysis of different silicene structures for 2D devices
summary: We report first-principles phonon dynamics studies in isotropically strained mono-layer silicene films of various topologies by density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory methods. The strain introduced in the sheets are of both tensile and compressive nature and its effect on the thermal transport properties are analysed using the Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) reported. We performed electronic and vibrational analysis of each silicene topology and concluded that hhk-silicene is a potential candidate for next generation electro-thermal devices due its molecular stability, bulk-Si like bandgap and tolerable thermal performance that can be engineered by strain. The novel hhk-silicene topology offers excellent thermal and electronic capabilities that are sensitive to strain along with the band gap following a near-linear monotonically decreasing trend making it suitable for strain-tronics applications.

title: Learning materials spectra across modalities and scales with structure-conditioned neural fields
summary: Spectroscopic observables encode rich information about material behavior across diverse, often high-dimensional domains of energy, momentum, and other experimental coordinates, providing critical insights into the physical properties underlying material functionalities and applications. However, learning these responses directly from atomic structures remains challenging due to the complexity of both structural configurations and spectroscopic observation spaces. Here, we develop a structure-conditioned neural-field framework that learns continuous spectroscopic response functions by coupling an equivariant structural encoder with a coordinate-conditioned network. The framework accurately predicts spectroscopic observables across diverse observation domains, ranging from one-dimensional densities of states to multidimensional scattering functions. We show that fine-tuning with limited spectral supervision captures strain- and composition-dependent spectral changes, with validated transfer to alloy configurations containing hundreds of atoms and computational scalability demonstrated for configurations exceeding $10^4$ atoms. Our work establishes a versatile and computationally scalable approach to learning structure-spectroscopy relationships, providing a foundation for spectroscopic analysis and future materials characterization, inverse problems, and experimental design.

title: Fredholm approximations to the Bethe-Salpeter equation with spherical-Bessel kernels for Wannier-Mott excitons
summary: We develop a deterministic radial approximation to the static Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE), designed for rapid preliminary screening of Wannier-Mott exciton binding across direct-gap bulk materials. The approximation replaces the electron-hole transition problem by small radial eigenvalue problems that require no stochastic sampling. Starting from the four-point BSE and its matrix representation in a Bloch electron-hole basis, we retain one valence and one conduction band in the effective-mass limit within the Tamm-Dancoff approximation. We introduce a central projection of the screened direct interaction and omit bare electron-hole exchange. The resulting model applies to spatially extended excitons whose envelopes vary slowly on the scale of the unit cell, provided that the effective-mass description and central screened interaction adequately represent the exciton of interest. A partial-wave decomposition separates the angular-momentum channels and expresses their interaction kernels as spherical-Bessel transforms of the real-space screened Coulomb interaction. Nystr\"{o}m discretization produces real symmetric radial matrices suitable for standard eigensolvers. Their dimension is set by the radial grid independently of the Brillouin-zone sampling used to calculate screening. We implement the formulation in the all-electron, full-potential code $\texttt{exciting}$. For bulk GaAs, the compact radial problem reproduces the corresponding conventional matrix-BSE binding energy within $(1~\mathrm{meV})$ at matched sampling. Further refinement achieves finite-mesh stability within the same tolerance on denser screening meshes without increasing the radial matrix size.

title: Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
summary: Conventional process optimization of the Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) growth parameters to achieve high-quality thin films relies on iterative, resource-intensive experimental runs. While predictive modeling can circumvent this cost and effort, simulating thin-film growth is constrained by the vastly different length and time scales of the deposition process. While continuum (e.g., Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)) and first-principles methods (e.g., Molecular Dynamics (MD)) struggle to balance experimental length/time scales and atomistic accuracy, Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) bridges this divide by resolving atomistic events whilst remaining tractable at experimental length and time scales. However, the accuracy of KMC relies on kinetic rate parameters that require costly density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In order to circumvent this, we present a framework that calibrates the rate parameters directly against experimental growth data. A forward KMC growth model is coupled in a closed loop with a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) optimizer that navigates the high-dimensional parameter space, with the search steered by the degree of rate control of each reaction rate parameter. The approach invokes no material-specific assumptions and hence, any deposition process whose forward kinetics can be reduced to a set of rate-controlled events is amenable to the same treatment. We demonstrate it for the MOCVD of GaAs, where the calibrated model captures the characteristic temperature dependence of the measured growth rate. The framework is also able to recover the three well known kinetic regimes characterized by change in the rate determining step from precursor chemisorption to desorption. As a result, the framework converts routinely measured growth data into a mechanistically interpretable model of the deposition process.

title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
summary: We investigated how the bias-voltage-dependent variation in the ferroelectric domain switching pathways affects the transient negative capacitance in multidomain PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains having, primarily, 90$^\circ$ walls. Using the vector piezoresponse force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, we show that, together with strain, local variation in composition results in the formation of labyrinthine domains in epitaxial films of thickness $\sim$1 $\mu$m. Clear signature of emergence of bias-voltage-dependent pathways could be observed in the Raman modes exhibiting splitting due to an intermediate state - different from the initial and final states - at the ``intermediate state of switching". The polarization relaxation patterns also show different states emerging depending on the bias voltage characteristics. The phase-field simulation of relaxation of ``intermediate state of switching" corroborates the experimental results and also exhibits dependence of the domain-wall area on the bias voltage and damping parameter. Combining the results of experiments and theoretical calculation, we show, therefore, that the variation of bias voltage leads to a change in the domain switching pathways and each pathway is associated with specific domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching". Since, the net domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching" governs the magnitude of transient negative capacitance, this work thus traces the origin of tunability of transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor.

title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
summary: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (35.9%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$
summary: Understanding and controlling the optical, thermal and mechanical properties of K$_2$PtCl$_6$-type double perovskites is essential for the design of lead-free, high-performance thermoelectric and optoelectronic materials. In this study, we investigate Cs$_2$SnI$_6$ using temperature-dependent near-resonance Raman scattering, complemented by density functional theory-based phonon calculations. The appearance of Raman-forbidden phonon modes in the Raman response at cryogenic temperatures provides strong evidence for local symmetry breaking that does not develop into a global structural phase transition. Through detailed analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and spectral lineshapes, we characterize the temperature evolution of the symmetry-broken structural response of Cs$_2$SnI$_6$. Below 200 K, multi-phonon scattering is strongly enhanced, and symmetry-forbidden Raman modes emerge. The temperature dependence of phonon intensities follows a phenomenological Arrhenius behavior, revealing an activation energy of 15-20 meV. These results establish temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy as a sensitive probe of local structural distortions and anharmonic structural dynamics in Cs$_2$SnI$_6$, providing a robust experimental basis for discussing the microscopic origins of symmetry breaking and electron-phonon coupling in halide double perovskites.

title: Symmetry-Based Transport Criterion and Robust Design for RuO$_2$-type Altermagnets
summary: Altermagnetism combines vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, enabling spin-transport functionalities without ferromagnetism. Although rutile RuO$_2$ has been proposed as a d-wave altermagnet, its magnetic ground state remains highly controversial. Moreover, existing transport verifications suffer from severe ambiguity due to the entanglement of spin-splitting effects and time-reversal-even spin-Hall contributions. Here, we introduce a two-pronged strategy to break the current verification impasse. First, we establish a definitive, symmetry-based transport criterion: by identifying specific crystallographic geometries where the spin-Hall background is strictly forbidden, we provide a zero-background window for unambiguous altermagnetic detection. Concurrently, to bypass the uncertain bulk energetics, we propose the RuO$_2$/MnO$_2$ superlattice as a prototypical platform to robustly enforce the d-wave altermagnetic order via interfacial magnetic proximity. Within this platform, symmetry-resolved spin-transport analysis reveals unconventional responses, including collinear spin currents enabling field-free magnetization switching and sizable spin-polarized charge currents. By combining a universal transport criterion with a robustly engineered material platform, our work transcends the debates over bulk properties, providing an actionable, definitive experimental roadmap for verifying d-wave altermagnetism.

title: Unoccupied spin texture of ordered Bi films on vicinal Ge substrates
summary: Vicinal surfaces offer a compelling testing ground in surface science: breaking the high symmetry of a singular surface introduces periodic step arrays that can modify surface states on the terraces and influence epitaxial ordering; the interplay between these effects governs morphology and electronic structure, especially in heavy, spin--orbit-coupled materials. We combine low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) and spin-polarized inverse photoemission (SP-IPES) with ab-initio calculations for the Bi$(1\,1\,1)$ reference, for the first time on a true high-index vicinal bismuth surface. On the ordered Bi$(9\,9\,11)$ vicinal film selected by Ge$(2\,2\,3)$, the measured unoccupied-state spin-sign sequence matches the calculated initial-state spectral function of Bi$(1\,1\,1)$ terraces. Conversely, the pseudo-cubic Bi domains retained on Ge$(4\,4\,3)$ and Ge$(3\,3\,1)$ exhibit a characteristic spin-polarized surface-state response referenced to the macroscopic vicinal surface. These results show that the substrate cut selects not only the morphology of the Bi film, but also the crystallographic reference frame of its unoccupied spin texture.

title: Accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth via tensor decomposition
summary: Phase-field models provide a powerful framework for simulating grain growth phenomena in polycrystalline materials, but their application to large-scale systems is limited by the high computational and memory costs associated with resolving multiple phase variables over fine spatial and temporal scales. This paper presents a tensor decomposition based model reduction framework for accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth. The proposed method exploits the underlying low-rank structure of the evolving phase-field variables and represents the high-dimensional solution in a spatially decomposed tensor format. By performing the numerical computations directly within this reduced representation, the framework decreases storage requirements and reduces the cost of repeatedly solving the phase-field equations. The number of modes for the decomposed approximation is controlled during the online computation with a subspace mode-updating algorithm, to balance computational efficiency and approximation accuracy. The method is assessed using representative grain growth problems, and its predictions are compared with those obtained from conventional full-order finite element simulations. The results demonstrate that the formulation can accurately reproduce the evolution of grain morphology and the principal characteristics of grain growth kinetics while substantially improving computational efficiency. The proposed framework therefore provides a promising approach for extending phase-field simulations to larger spatial domains, finer discretizations, and systems containing a large number of phase variables.

title: Theory of the charge response of the boron-vacancy spin in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride
summary: The boron vacancy $V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$ in hexagonal boron nitride is a leading two-dimensional spin sensor, but the microscopic connection between nearby charge positions and its spin Hamiltonian remains poorly understood. Calculations for carbon and oxygen donors 3.85--8.08 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ away show that direction matters, not only distance. In the frozen lattice, reversing a carbon donor's azimuth at 4.35 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ (C1 to C1m) more than halves $|E|$ and turns its axis across the mirror line. The ratio is 0.467 with the Perdew--Burke--Ernzerhof (PBE) functional, against 1 for distance alone. A field-plus-gradient model fitted to six donor configurations, including C1 but excluding C1m, predicted a ratio of 0.443 before C1m was calculated. Heyd--Scuseria--Ernzerhof hybrid statics give 0.432 and PBE relaxation 0.600. Exploratory analysis suggests why direction matters: a charge's potential differs at the three vacancy nitrogens and moves the spin of the two $e'$ holes among them, more when the charge faces one nitrogen than the gap between two. $E$ follows this spin imbalance through one constant, $c\approx8$ GHz per $\mu_{\mathrm{B}}$, across donors and applied fields, whereas in PBE $D$ is nearly insensitive to it. A three-site model with one fitted screening constant reproduces the frozen-lattice $E$ to 83 MHz rms. Results are for one charge state in a free-standing monolayer; absolute $|E|$ varies by tens of percent across approximations.

title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
summary: Refractory compositionally complex alloys (R-CCAs) show great promise as next generation structural materials for extreme conditions, but alloys with excellent high temperature mechanical properties most often exhibit virtually zero room temperature tensile ductility, hindering potential commercial application. Several semi-empirical metrics have been employed for predicting plasticity in R-CCAs, including valence electron concentration, Pugh ratio, Rice criteria, and the D-parameter. While many currently available ductility metrics correlate very well when compressive plasticity is considered, only the density functional theory (DFT) based D-parameter shows a strong correlation in tension. A new ductility metric is developed using CALculation of PHAse Diagrams (CALPHAD) thermodynamics, Gamma, with includes the free energy difference between the body-centered cubic (BCC) and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) phases, the interfacial free energy of a (110) BCC surface, and an electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion. The Gamma parameter exhibits better correlation with tensile ductility than D-parameter and performs equally well in compression. While this improvement is modest, a thermodynamically grounded ductility metric is clearly required to capture intrinsic ductility behavior. Extrinsic contributions to brittle behavior in R-CCAs, namely interstitial oxygen content, are also briefly discussed. Combining the Gamma ductility parameter with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility is proposed as a first order attempt to capture both intrinsic and extrinsic contributions to ductile behavior in R-CCAs.

title: Ferroelectric Switching in x-cut MgO-doped Thin-Film Lithium Niobate: Implications for Periodic Poling and Domain-Wall Electronics
summary: Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) revives a mature ferroelectric as a wafer-scale platform for integrated photonics and, increasingly, for domain-wall electronics such as nonvolatile memories and memristors. Both applications rely on controlled ferroelectric switching, which is poorly understood in TFLN: periodic poling consistently requires electric fields above 30~kV/mm, far above the coercive fields of about 21~kV/mm and 4.5~kV/mm of bulk congruent and 5~mol\% MgO-doped lithium niobate, respectively. Here, we present systematic ferroelectric hysteresis measurements on x-cut, 5~mol\% MgO-doped TFLN with coplanar electrodes as used for periodic poling, combining the positive-up-negative-down (PUND) method with second-harmonic microscopy (SHM). We obtain a spontaneous polarization of $(0.72\pm0.02)$~C/m$^2$, consistent with bulk values, while the coercive field varies between 24 and 40~kV/mm with the voltage ramp rate and depends on the electrode geometry. We identify three contributions to the high coercive fields: (i) fast voltage ramps, (ii) finger electrodes, and (iii) the coplanar surface-electrode geometry. Together with bulk data, the coercive field follows a single power law of the ramp rate over five orders of magnitude, showing that the high fields are dominated by switching dynamics rather than by intrinsic thin-film properties. Moreover, the apparent internal field depends on the electrode geometry, and reverse switching leaves buried, electrically isolated domains. These results provide guidelines for scalable, fab-compatible periodic poling---one of the principal bottlenecks of TFLN device integration---and for the write and erase operation of TFLN domain-wall devices.

title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
summary: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. The different core-level shifts and band offsets indicate that the electronic structure is sensitive to the interfacial bonding and electrostatic environment introduced by the two integration schemes. These results demonstrate that, even for an identical Si/Ge material pair, the interface-formation pathway provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling heterojunction band alignment, offering a route toward interface-engineered electronic and optoelectronic devices.

title: Defect Chemistry of Hafnia-Based Ferroelectrics under Oxide-Electrode Constraints
summary: HfO$_2$ heterostructures with La$_{0.67}$Sr$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$ (LSMO) epitaxial electrodes have attracted interest as ferroelectric systems with electrode-dependent defect chemistry. However, the formation and stability of defects under LSMO-constrained chemical conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we use density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate oxygen vacancies and La-, Sr-, and Mn-related interstitial and substitutional defects in HfO$_2$ under chemical environments constrained by the LSMO electrode. We find that LSMO stability substantially narrows the accessible O chemical potential range relative to bulk HfO$_2$, altering the predicted defect formation energies. While La and Sr substitutional defects are governed primarily by preferred ionic valence states, oxygen vacancies and Mn substitutional defects exhibit charge states sensitive to the local atomic environment. In addition, defect-complex calculations in orthorhombic HfO$_2$ reveal negative binding energies, indicating favorable defect association. The La- and Mn-related defect complexes exhibit thermodynamic competition, with their relative stability depending on the Fermi level and oxygen chemical potential. Lastly, extending the analysis to Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ and ZrO$_2$ reveals common oxygen-vacancy trends, while the stability of LSMO-derived defects depends more strongly on the host material and crystal phase. These results provide a thermodynamic basis for understanding how electrode-constrained chemical environments and host structures influence defect formation, charge compensation, and defect-complex stability in HfO$_2$-based materials.

title: Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
summary: We performed Shubnikov--de Haas (SdH) oscillation measurements on the $\mathbf{Q}=0$ antiferromagnet NbMnP, which exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect. The SdH frequencies observed in the low-field region up to 17.5~T are well described by first-principles band-structure calculations based on the $B_{3g}+B_{2u}$ noncollinear magnetic structure determined by neutron diffraction. The effective masses are enhanced by approximately a factor of two relative to the calculated band masses. High-field measurements up to 41.5~T reveal a Lifshitz transition accompanied by a pronounced evolution of the SdH frequency spectrum. These results confirm that first-principles calculations provide a reliable tool for the development of functional antiferromagnetic materials, while also demonstrating that field-induced changes in the Fermi surface itself need to be taken into account in understanding their high-field magnetotransport properties.

title: The effect of local stacking fault fluctuations on dislocation glide and the interplay with solid solution strengthening in Al-Mg alloys
summary: Concentrated alloys are characterized by a random arrangement of solute atoms of different sizes, which generates spatially fluctuating displacement and stress fields with non-trivial correlations. This chemical disorder also induces local fluctuations in stacking-fault (SF) energies, giving rise to fluctuating SF forces acting on the partial dislocations bounding the SF. In this work, we investigate the characteristics of the SF noise, including spatial correlations and the impact of such SF energy fluctuations on dislocation glide. Specifically, the gliding behavior of screw, edge, and mixed dislocations in a model concentrated Al-Mg random alloy with varying Mg content is analyzed. The interplay between SF energy fluctuations and solid-solution noise is also discussed. We show that SF forces are spatially correlated, in close analogy with long-range elastic stresses, and exhibit a robust negative correlation along the slip direction. We identify the physical origin of these correlations and demonstrate that they significantly contribute to the critical resolved shear stress for dislocations to glide. In contrast, correlations in other directions are weaker but can still be non-negligible, depending on the underlying interatomic interactions.

title: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the Mo-S-Al-O System
summary: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the Mo-S-Al-O system, targeting MoS$_2$ heteroepitaxy on c-plane sapphire, $\alpha$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001). The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from about 1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) configurations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On held-out data, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/$\mathring{A}$. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5%, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of edges, point defects (Spearman $\rho$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($\rho$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($\rho$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %. The resulting potential enables future studies of the atomic-scale mechanisms of defect formation in two-dimensional heteroepitaxy.

title: Moir\'e reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
summary: Twisted oxide double layers have emerged as a promising platform for exploring moir\'e physics, including polar topologies and emergent electronic phases. However, the intrinsic complexity of oxide surfaces, such as contamination, roughness, and the presence of two distinct terminations (AO and BO2), can complicate the identification of buried interfacial structures. Here, using atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a predominantly SrO-TiO2 interfacial configuration, we directly visualize a moir\'e-periodic structural reconstruction at the buried interface that is distinct from the geometric moir\'e of rigid stacking. The reconstructed interface hosts head-to-head-like polar distortions, moir\'e-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance in otherwise paraelectric and insulating SrTiO3. Our work demonstrates that, with a well-defined termination, moir\'e reconstruction could serve as a route to emergent electrical behavior in twisted perovskite oxides.

title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
summary: Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.

title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
summary: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations with classical path approximation (CPA-NAMD) cannot simulate the carrier dynamics under an external field. We develop CPA-NAMD-extF, a first-principles density-matrix framework for calculating field-driven electronic responses along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories. The method combines explicit external-field coupling with self-consistent updates of electronic density while retaining the computational efficiency of the classical-path approximation. Benchmarks against regular TDDFT methods show close agreement for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses. Applications to the linear absorption spectrum of crystalline and amorphous SiO$_2$ demonstrate its capability to large and structurally complex systems. This method is also applied to the 2D hybrid perovskite $(\mathrm{BA})_2\mathrm{CsPb}_2\mathrm{Br}_7$. Finite-temperature calculations show that the second-order opto-current response is strongly affected by structural fluctuations. Real-space DC current density further reveals pronounced Br-centered vortex currents, and its microscopic origin is investigated.

title: Collective dipole effects amplify field-driven ion transport in amorphous Li$_3$PO$_4$
summary: Amorphous solid electrolytes often outperform their crystalline counterparts, but how disorder shapes ionic transport under strong electric fields is poorly understood. We use molecular dynamics with a machine-learned interatomic potential and a machine-learned Born-effective-charge model to measure Li mobility in amorphous Li$_3$PO$_4$ and in a crystal with Li vacancies, from the linear to the strongly nonlinear regime. The amorphous phase shows a much stronger field enhancement, and we trace this to a collective dipole effect. The migrating ion carries the same charge in both phases. Alone it would not make the amorphous phase respond more strongly. What makes the difference is the environment. In the amorphous network the surrounding atoms move with the hop. Their motion makes the work the field performs vary widely between hops. Since hopping rates grow exponentially with the work, the most strongly assisted hops can dominate the drift. Disorder thus enhances field-driven transport through the environment rather than the carrier itself, a mechanism that may operate in disordered ion conductors in general.

title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. Using an energy-path determination procedure, the diffusion barriers were obtained as the difference between the initial site energy and the activated complex state energy. The detachment energy of the NM adatom was obtained assuming a final state in atomic and molecular form. The energy barrier for detachment to the atomic state is high for all atoms, on the order of 5 eV. For the molecular state these barriers are different: smaller for nitrogen, on the order of 1 eV, which is related to the high dissociation energy of the N2 molecule. For P and As the barrier is above 2 eV. For Sb it was not determined. Accordingly, the surface diffusion length is macroscopically large, indicating that all NM adatoms arrive at the steps.

title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
summary: Rare-earth nickelates are among the most active oxide electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), owing to their tunable Ni-O covalency, near-unity eg occupancy, and sensitivity to A-site chemistry, oxygen stoichiometry, and epitaxial strain. Here, we use epitaxial A-site high-entropy (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 thin films to reveal how epitaxial strain influences defect formation, Ni valence, electronic structure, and OER activity in a chemically disordered rare-earth (RE) sublattice. Tensile strain promotes Ruddlesden-Popper fault formation, interrupts the corner-sharing NiO6 network, and lowers the average Ni oxidation state. Although the occupied density of states near the Fermi level remains largely unchanged, O K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveals increased low-energy unoccupied states under tensile strain. First-principles calculations suggest that tensile strain shifts RE 4f-derived states toward the Fermi level, enhancing RE 4f-O 2p-Ni 3d hybridization. These coupled structural and electronic changes lead to earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates. The high-entropy nickelate also shows enhanced resistance to OER-induced structural degradation compared with LaNiO3. These results suggest that A-site configurational disorder and epitaxial strain can jointly tune defect formation and rare-earth-derived electronic states, providing a route for improving perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.

title: Magnetic order in Co[Cr(CN)$_6$]$_{2/3}\cdot z$H$_2$O and its interplay with correlated vacancy order
summary: Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) are versatile hybrid framework materials that often exhibit local and long-range departures from their cubic parent structure, influencing their functionality. Long-range magnetic order is common in PBAs, owing to magnetic interactions between transition metal ions via bridging cyanide ligands in the structure. Here we report the magnetic structure of cobalt (II) hexacyanochromate, Co[Cr(CN)$_6$]$_{2/3}\cdot z$H$_2$O, determined using neutron powder diffraction. No evidence for magnetostriction at the magnetic ordering temperature is observed in contrast to the reported behaviour of a related PBA. Following experimental characterisation of the magnetic order of this PBA, we employ a simple Monte Carlo model to gain a better understanding of the relationship between hexacyanometallate vacancy distributions and magnetic ordering behaviour in these materials. This model shows that magnetic ordering is robust to the extent and nature of vacancy correlations, with only minor effects noticeable in the critical region, suggesting that PBAs with the same composition but different vacancy correlations might be expected to show similar magnetic behaviour.

title: Molecular Curvature Enables Tubular {\pi}-Stacked Pathways in Three-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Frameworks
summary: Conductive metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are commonly constructed from planar aromatic ligands, whose geometries favor conventional {\pi}-stacking arrangements. However, intrinsically twisted ligands offer an alternative geometric approach to directing aromatic packing and constructing unconventional framework architectures. Here, we employ intrinsically twisted, butterfly-shaped dibenzo[g,p]chrysene-2,3,6,7,10,11,14,15-octaol (DBC) ligands to construct a series of lanthanide MOFs. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals an interpenetrated three-dimensional framework in which {\pi}-{\pi} interactions between the aromatic fragments generate axially extended tubular {\pi}-stacked pathways, alongside one-dimensional channels rich in hydrogen-bonding sites. Lanthanide substitution preserves the overall tubular framework topology while modulating aromatic stacking distances and local pore environments. PrDBC single crystals exhibit mixed electron-proton transport, with electron and proton conductivities reaching 1.62 x 10-3 and 4.37 x 10-4 S cm-1, respectively, at 338 K and 30% relative humidity. This work highlights molecular curvature as a structural design strategy for constructing three-dimensional conductive MOFs that integrate tubular aromatic stacks with tunable pore environments for mixed electron-proton transport.

title: Anion Engineering Enables Concurrent Optimization of Phonon and Carrier Transport in AMg$_2$X$_2$ Zintl Thermoelectrics
summary: The simultaneous suppression of lattice heat transport and enhancement of carrier transport is central to the development of high-performance thermoelectric materials. Here, we investigate the microscopic mechanisms governing phonon and carrier transport in CaAl$_2$Si$_2$-type AMg$_2$X$_2$ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = P, As, Sb, Bi) Zintl compounds using first-principles calculations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport theory. As X changes from P to Bi, the widening phonon band gap restricts three-phonon scattering channels and increases the relative importance of four-phonon processes. In CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ and BaMg$_2$Bi$_2$, four-phonon scattering dominates the relaxation of low-frequency heat-carrying modes at 900 K. The Bi-based series also exhibits an anomalous increase in lattice thermal conductivity from Ca to Ba despite the increasing cation mass. Mode-resolved analysis links the lower thermal conductivity of CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ to reduced low-frequency group velocities and stronger anharmonic scattering, with Ca-related mid-frequency vibrations providing additional four-phonon scattering channels. Including both particle-like and coherent contributions, its lattice thermal conductivity reaches 0.23 W$\cdot$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$ at 900 K. Meanwhile, the increasing covalent character of the vertical Mg-X bonds is accompanied by enhanced band-edge dispersion and reduced carrier effective masses. These electronic changes, together with conduction-band convergence, favor n-type transport and yield a predicted peak $ZT$ of 3.68 at 900 K in CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$. These results elucidate the interplay of phonon spectral structure and higher-order anharmonicity in thermal transport, alongside the distinct electronic response to anion substitution.

title: Ultrafast Polar Topology Reversal via THz-Driven Inertial Switching
summary: Topological polar structures in ferroelectric heterostructures offer functional states beyond ordinary domains. As polarization reversal underpins ferroelectric devices, switching between degenerate topological variants, which we refer to as topology reversal, would greatly expand the ways to control polar textures. However, polar topology reversal is challenging because it requires coordinated flipping of oppositely oriented local polarizations, a process not naturally driven by a uniform electric field. Using a multiscale modeling approach, we show that polar topology can be stabilized and reversed in a simple Pt/PbTiO$_3$/Pt nanocapacitor. Electrode-controlled boundary conditions drive tetragonal PbTiO$_3$ into competing orthorhombic- and rhombohedral-like polarization states, which form building blocks for diverse topological structures, including vortex arrays, skyrmion lattices, dipole spirals, and dipole waves. We further show that the same out-of-plane THz pulse can reversibly switch a double-$\mathbf q$ dipole wave between degenerate topological variants within a few picoseconds, while preserving its spatial modulation. This process is enabled by damping-assisted inertial switching, in which the THz pulse injects energy to drive large-angle polarization rotation across shallow barriers, while dissipation removes excess energy and traps the system in the reversed state. These results establish ferroelectric nanocapacitors as a simple platform for programmable polar topology and low-power, THz-speed control through dissipative dynamics.

title: Characterisation of surface layers formed on plasma-facing components in controlled fusion devices: Role of heavy ion elastic recoil detection
summary: Wall components retrieved from the TEXTOR tokamak after tracer experiments with nitrogen-15 and molybdenum hexafluoride (MoF6) injection were studied to determine deposition patterns and, by this, to conclude on material migration. Toroidal limiter tiles made of carbon fibre composites and fine grain graphite were examined using time-of-flight heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis. Molybdenum deposition patterns indicated migration based on erosion and prompt re-deposition. Nitrogen-15 was trapped together with the deposited molybdenum. Some information on the depth distribution of species in the top 400 nm layer of the limiters was obtained; however surface roughness of the samples strongly limited resolution. In the case of molybdenum, the largest concentration was found in the 100 nm outermost layer, whereas fluorine and nitrogen-15 displayed more irregular profiles. Other species, besides deuterium fuel and carbon-12, were also identified: boron-10 and boron-11 originating from boronisations, carbon-13 from earlier tracer experiments, nitrogen-14 from plasma edge cooling and metals eroded from the Inconel wall.

title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
summary: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

title: Pressure-correlation phase diagram unraveling quantum phase transitions in altermagnetic $\epsilon$-FeOOH and realization of piezo-anomalous Hall effect
summary: We establish a pressure-correlation phase diagram that yields multiple pressure-tunable quantum phase transitions in iron oxyhydroxide ($\epsilon$-FeOOH) across three critical pressures, $P_{c1}>P_{c2}>P_{c3}$. The transitions arise from the competition among electron-correlation, crystal-field, and Hund's coupling. First-principles calculations reveal that the earlier reported high-spin (HS) to low-spin (LS) crossover at correlation-sensitive $P_{c1}$ is accompanied by a transition from charge-transfer to Mott insulating (CTI-MI) phase, and a change in the spin-quantization axis (SQA) from $\hat{y}$ to $\hat{x}$. The HS-LS crossover and CTI-MI transition is driven by the simultaneous increase in crystal-field splitting and decrease in Hund's coupling. The critical pressure $P_{c2}$ governing the structural transition from centrosymmetric $Pnnm$ phase to noncentrosymmetric $P2_1nm$ phase is found to be independent of electron-correlation. When correlation is strong, a third critical pressure ($P_{c3}$) emerges in the lower-pressure regime of the phase diagram. Validating the recent experimental observation, $P_{c3}$ is responsible for changing the SQA from $\hat{z}$ to $\hat{y}$. By exhibiting altermagnetism in both $P2_1nm$ and $Pnnm$ phases and possessing finite anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) only for SQA along $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$, $\epsilon$-FeOOH enables a unique piezo-anomalous Hall effect where one can switch on the AHC at a lower pressure and change its direction at a higher pressure.

title: Piezogyration and elastogyration in ternary chalcopyrites from first principles
summary: Natural optical activity arises from the spatial dispersion of the optical response and is described by the rank-two gyration pseudotensor. Its dependence on mechanical stress and strain, quantified by the piezogyration and elastogyration tensors, respectively, has been investigated experimentally for decades. However, a systematic first-principles description of these effects remains largely unexplored. Here we present a first-principles methodology to compute the full piezogyration and elastogyration tensors, and apply it to a set of representative ternary chalcopyrite crystals. The gyration of the unstrained crystal turns out to be a poor predictor of the magnitude of the elastogyration response, which we find to be a property inherited from their parent zinc-blende structures. The elastic compliance tensor further shapes the piezogyration response, with particularly pronounced effects in AgGaS$_2$, a well-known achiral yet optically active crystal. Finally, we explore strain-induced chirality through the trace of the gyration tensor, the only pseudoscalar contribution to the natural optical activity that is linear in the tensor components and encodes information about chirality.

title: Amplitude-conserving frequency demultiplexer based on a spin wave delay line
summary: Propagating spin waves have emerged as promising candidates for signal processing and information transmission. We present a theoretical investigation of the generation, propagation and collection of spin-wave wave packets in micrometer-wide magnetic conduits, highlighting their potential for analogue frequency demultiplexing in space and time. We clarify the roles of the excitation duration and of the spin wave dispersion relation, as well as the influence of the spin-wave linewidth in setting the spatio-temporal evolution of propagating spin-wave wavepackets excited by Gaussian field pulses. We issue rules for the spatio-temporal separation of wavepackets that carry different frequencies. We finally propose an amplitude-conserving frequency demultiplexer based on a spin wave delay line of 60x5 $\mu$m$^2$ footprint.

title: Local and itinerant orbital contributions to the gyromagnetic response of paramagnetic metals
summary: Orbitronics exploits orbital angular momentum to generate and manipulate angular-momentum currents for controlling magnetisation, offering new approaches to magnetic memory and logic. A quantitative description of this process requires establishing how orbital angular momentum contributes to magnetic moments and, consequently, to the gyromagnetic response that governs magnetisation dynamics. Here, we present a first-principles framework for calculating the effective gyromagnetic tensor (g') of paramagnetic metals, consistently incorporating local and itinerant orbital contributions, spin-orbit coupling, and both state- and occupation-change effects. Applying the framework to V and Pt, we find that orbital paramagnetic responses are comparable to or larger than spin contributions and substantially modify g' from the free-electron value. The atom-centered approximation can underestimate the orbital response by approximately a factor of two, while neglecting occupation changes produces significant errors in the calculated g'. Our calculated g' values for V and Pt agree with experiment, while their pronounced dependence on band filling reveals a route to engineering angular-momentum responses through electronic-structure control. The results establish the modern theory of orbital magnetism as an essential ingredient for describing gyromagnetic response and provide a framework for identifying materials with enhanced orbital functionalities.

title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
summary: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned N\'eel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Thermodynamic stability at high pressure and dynamical stability at ambient pressure indicate that it can be made by the route established for this family.

title: Fabry-P\'erot Cavity formed by Magnonic waveguide using holes and notches
summary: In this paper, we have investigated a spin-wave-based Fabry-P\'erot (FP) cavity using two air holes and notches embedded in a magnonic waveguide. Through micromagnetic simulations, we have demonstrated the spin-wave profile, as well as the transmission and reflection spectra of the FP type magnonic waveguide, by varying the distance between the center of holes and notches. We have introduced an analysis of the reflection spectra in an FP type magnonic waveguide, which is essential and considerable for the performance of magnonic integrated circuits. We have also presented a theoretical model to describe the transmission and reflection characteristics of the FP-type magnonic waveguide. Furthermore, active tuning of the resonance peak of the FP type magnonic wavguide by varying the external magnetic field has been demonstrated. Our proposed structure and its study may contribute to the development of magnonic integrated circuits for low-power computing and data processing in next-generation spintronic technologies.

title: Dysfunctional Functionals and their Therapies in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
summary: The exchange-correlation functional in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) is known to have dependence on past densities and initial states, and yet this memory-dependence is ignored in practical calculations which almost always use an adiabatic approximation. We discuss the dysfunction that arises due to this deficiency and point to therapies that go beyond the adiabatic approximation. Still, adiabatic TDDFT has had success in a wide range of systems for response properties and for fully non-equilibrium dynamics, and why this is so is only partially understood. This, together with the rigorous foundation of the exact theory and its favorable system-size scaling, provides tremendous impetus for continuing to strive towards improved approximations to the exact functionals, and a deeper understanding of the impact of approximations in applications.

title: RIXS study of strain-tuned coupled valence and spin-state transition in epitaxial $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ films
summary: Strain-tuned $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ thin films provide a model system for controlling coupled valence, spin-state, structural and metal-insulator transitions (VSSTs) in perovskite cobaltite materials. Here, we use Co $L_{2,3}$ and Pr $M_{4,5}$ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), along with Co $L_{3}$ edge Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS), to probe the local electronic structure across the strain-controlled VSST in epitaxial (Pr,Y,Ca)CoO$_{3}$ thin films. In compressively strained films on YAlO$_{3}$ (YAO) substrates, cooling through the transition produces Pr$^{4+}$-like spectral weight, suppresses Co$^{4+}$-like character, and favors predominantly low-spin Co$^{3+}$. The changes at the Pr and Co edges are quantitatively consistent with a reduction of approximately 0.15 holes per Co in the Co--O network. By contrast, tensile-strained thin films on La$_{0.18}$Sr$_{0.82}$Al$_{0.59}$Ta$_{0.41}$O$_{3}$ (LSAT) substrates have nearly temperature-independent spectra. Multiplet calculations reproduce the principal XAS lineshapes and local $dd$ excitations at high energy loss. Additionally, low-energy RIXS intensity recovered above the transition is consistent with a combination of Co$^{4+}$-like local excitations and a broader particle--hole continuum associated with the metallic phase. These results provide element-resolved evidence for charge compensation between the Pr and Co--O sublattices and support cooperative coupling among charge-transfer, spin-state, and lattice structure at the strain-controlled VSST.

title: Zeeman Spin Photocurrents without Spin Textures
summary: Inversion symmetry forbids bulk second-order spin photocurrents driven solely by electric-dipole coupling. We show that interference between the electric-dipole and spin Zeeman couplings of light enables Zeeman spin-shift and spin-injection currents in centrosymmetric magnets. Our microscopic theory and systematic symmetry analysis establish the allowed responses and polarization selection rules for both spin-degenerate and spin-split antiferromagnets, with and without spin--orbit coupling (SOC). In collinear magnets without SOC, spin injection vanishes, whereas a pure spin-shift current survives independently of the carrier scattering time. This response arises from transverse electronic spin coherences generated by the optical magnetic field, while the ordered moments remain collinear and fixed. Model analyses validate the mechanism, and first-principles calculations for $\mathrm{MnF_2}$ predict experimentally accessible spin photocurrents. These findings establish a general framework for optical spin-current generation in centrosymmetric magnets, including a SOC-free pure-spin mechanism particularly relevant to altermagnets.

title: Graph-Covariant Bottom-Up Scale-Bridging Reconstruction of Ground and Excited States of Extended Systems
summary: We propose a hierarchical scale-bridging construction for building first principles electronic structure models of extended molecular aggregates with disorder, and its practical realization in exciton systems. The general construction, referred here as to the encapsulation, is based on a recursive operator-valued hierarchy cast in a dual graph-theoretic (discrete) and configuration-space (continuous) structure, in which variables associated with a coarser level parameterize operators governing the degrees of freedom at the next finer level in a graph-covariant, geometry-preserving fashion. In an exemplary application of this scheme, aggregate-level ground- and excited-state operators are constructed through a many-body expansion (MBE), with matrix elements evaluated in a basis comprising the aggregate ground state and local Frenkel excitations. The required monomer and dimer building blocks are obtained from DFT and TDDFT calculations, yielding aggregate-level 1-particle transition density matrices as well as Hamiltonian, dipole moment and other operators that can be evaluated at the level of the building blocks. Starting from structural models obtained from experiment or molecular dynamics, this approach generates aggregate-level operators in a bottom-up fashion without fitting parameters to spectroscopic data or performing calculations on larger system cutouts. A numerical demonstration is given for an excitonic manifold in crystalline quaterthiophene. In particular, through its intrinsic configuration-dependence encoded in the encapsulations, it will provide a bridge between static electronic structure calculations for realistic, structurally disordered aggregates and quantum or quantum-classical simulations of exciton-vibrational dynamics.

title: Theoretical Prediction of Superconducting 2D Hydrogenated Janus V2CSH and Nb2CSH MXenes
summary: Two dimensional hydrogenated Janus MXenes represent a new frontier in superconducting materials, where asymmetric surface terminations enable tunable electronic and vibrational properties. In this work, we present the first comparative study of hydrogen or sulfur terminated V2CSH and Nb2CSH monolayers using density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory. Both compounds are structurally and thermally stable, exhibiting isotropic in plane elasticity and nonmagnetic multiband metallic states dominated by transition metal d orbitals. The asymmetric S or H terminations generate nonequivalent surface potentials and intrinsic out of plane dipoles. Electron phonon coupling constants of 0.39 (V2CSH) and 0.53 (Nb2CSH) yield superconducting transition temperatures of 2.36 K and 5.27 K, respectively, within the Allen Dynes framework. Low energy lattice vibrations, primarily involving metal and sulfur atoms, account for 77% of the coupling in both MXenes. These findings establish metal substitution as a design principle for tuning superconductivity in Janus MXenes and highlight Nb2CSH as a promising candidate for low temperature superconducting applications.

title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
summary: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.

title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
summary: Generative models for crystal structure prediction (CSP) have expanded the search space for novel materials and improved screening efficiency. However, simultaneously generating stable and novel structures remains challenging because of the complex structural and physical constraints governing crystals. To address this challenge, we propose site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer model (ST2M), a symmetry-guided discrete--continuous diffusion framework incorporating degree-of-freedom masks and conditioned on Wyckoff patterns. ST2M represents crystal structures as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits and employs a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables. In our experiments, ST2M achieves a structural validity of 96.37\%. For known patterns in dataset, 23.86\% of generated structures simultaneously satisfy stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria, representing a relative improvement of 68.15\% over the best-performing baseline. First-principles calculations identify a total of 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected candidates with low predicted energies. These results demonstrate that ST2M can generate chemically viable crystal candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints and generalize to unknown Wyckoff patterns, providing a practical route to accelerated materials discovery.

title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
summary: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit. Non-dimensional scaling brings all governing coefficients within one decade of O(1), and the setup removes the boundary and initial-condition penalty weights that soft-constraint methods must tune. In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise), a soft-penalty baseline with adaptive weights converges to an erroneous $e_{15}$ in four of the five runs (51.7% mean error), and fixed penalties reach an error of 0.85% only after a second-order optimization stage. The constrained formulations reach mean $e_{15}$ errors between 0.15% and 0.51% with held-out displacement errors below 1%. Within these variants, the spatial multiplier gives rapid first-order convergence, and the quadratic temporal multiplier lowers the early-time electrostatic residual by a factor of 6.8 versus a linear one. On finite-element data along one subsurface line, the full formulation recovers $e_{15}$ with 1.19% mean error at 30 dB and keeps it between 0.65% and 2.71% across a 40 to 0 dB noise sweep. Finally, training on displacements alone still recovers $e_{15}$ with mean errors of 0.45% on finite-element and 1.64% on manufactured data.

title: A Julia implementation of Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation in periodic systems
summary: We present a flexible Julia codebase implementing Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation (HHG) in periodic tight-binding systems. Using the frequency-domain Fourier-Sambe formalism, the package maps the time-dependent Schroedinger equation onto a static eigenvalue problem. This allows direct computation of Floquet states, quasienergy bands, and harmonic currents for 1D, 2D, or 3D lattices under arbitrary light polarizations. The implementation supports both analytical Fourier-Bessel expansions (via Peierls substitution) and numerical Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT). We validate the code against a canonical 1D two-band model and showcase its capabilities on 2D honeycomb systems: gapped graphene mapping HHG cutoff scaling with hopping parameters and the Kane-Mele model, exploring field-induced quasienergy gaps and topological transitions under linear and circular driving fields. In addition to the theoretical presentation, we provide a flexible and efficient open-source Julia implementation of the Floquet formalism: https://github.com/Ashwin-A-Pillai/Floquet-Fourier-Numericals/tree/main.

title: Anomalous response, re-emerging localization-transition and robust corner sates in self-similar peano fractal
summary: Anomalous spectral response from the non-interacting electrons on a peano fractal is recorded within tight-binding framework. It is observed that a minimal off-diagonal anisotropy can modulate the transport characteristics of the lattice. Drastic modification in the nature of the eigenstates has been validated through the workout of level spacing statistics. Further, a two-dimensional quasiperiodic Aubry-Andr\'e and Harper variation in the overlap integral can invite re-entrant localization-delocalization transition for the self-similar model. This is associated with the possible existence of single-particle mobility edge in the energy landscape. Our results are corroborated by the evaluation of inverse participation ratio, fractal dimension and quantum dynamical response. The spectrum is shown to formulate a quantum butterfly pattern with the frequency of the modulation. Chiral symmetry protected edge states are found to be insensitive with respect to moderate diagonal disorder.

title: Galilean electrodynamics fluctuation in a superfluid: from general coordinate invariance to Tkachenko mode
summary: We explore coupling the Galilean electrodynamics (GED) to an s-wave superfluid. Governed by the general coordinate invariance, the proposed effective Lagrangian hosts an unconventional superfluid whose mass is shifted by the GED gauge multiplet.
